digest.en: Russia and Ukraine have announced rival ceasefires. Deadly strikes continue despite the announcements. Europe's car industry is meanwhile at the centre of a new US trade war.
digest.hi: विदेशी रिपोर्ट में खुलासा हुआ है कि भारत ने घर में घुसकर पाकिस्तान को मारा था। ऑपरेशन सिंदूर की सच्चाई सामने आई है। इस घटना ने भारत और पाकिस्तान के बीच तनाव को बढ़ा दिया है।

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine announce rival ceasefires as deadly strikes continue
articles.summary: Russia and Ukraine announced rival ceasefires, with Ukraine pausing fighting sooner to pin violations on Moscow. Russia demanded a ceasefire on 8 and 9 May but Ukraine said it would pause the fighting sooner, meaning any violations would be pinned on Moscow.

articles.title: Hegseth says ceasefire is not over despite Iranian strikes on UAE and commercial vessels
articles.summary: Iranian strikes hit the UAE and commercial vessels, despite a claimed ceasefire, according to Hegseth. Live updates: Hegseth says ceasefire is not over despite Iranian strikes on UAE and commercial vessels AP News.

articles.title: U.S. and Iran Both Claim Control Over Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: The US and Iran claim control over the Strait of Hormuz, with the US escorting ships and Iran intensifying control. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth hailed the new U. S. initiative to escort ships through the waterway, but traffic has not resumed.

articles.title: Venice Biennale in crisis: The controversies explained
articles.summary: The Venice Biennale will not award the Golden Lion due to jury resignation over Russia and Israel's participation. The traditional Golden Lion will not be awarded this year, following the resignation of the jury over Russia's and Israel's disputed participation.

articles.title: Why Europe’s car industry is at the centre of a new US trade war
articles.summary: The US may increase tariffs on EU cars and trucks to 25 percent, threatening Europe's car industry. Trump has threatened to increase tariffs on EU cars and trucks exported to the US from 15 percent to 25 percent.

articles.title: Why Iran can’t afford to give up Hormuz control
articles.summary: Iran relies heavily on the Strait of Hormuz for leverage in negotiations with Washington. The passageway is vital for Tehran, and giving up control would undermine its bargaining power. The vital passageway is key for Tehran as it seeks to leverage in negotiations with Washington.

articles.title: What Ghana’s foreign-built landmarks tell us about its global relationships
articles.summary: Ghana's foreign-built landmarks reveal its global relationships. The structures, built by countries like China and the US, demonstrate the nation's diplomatic and economic ties. What Ghana’s foreign-built landmarks tell us about its global relationships The Conversation.

articles.title: Cruise Ship Struck by Hantavirus Is to Head to Canary Islands, W.H.O. Says
articles.summary: A cruise ship with a hantavirus outbreak will head to the Canary Islands. The World Health Organization reported possible human-to-human transmission, and Spain will decide on a port after disease experts inspect the vessel.

articles.title: Hegseth says 'ceasefire is not over' as US and Tehran struggle for control of Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: A ceasefire may not be over in the Strait of Hormuz. The US and Tehran are struggling for control, with Hegseth warning that the situation remains volatile. Iran war live: Hegseth says 'ceasefire is not over' as US and Tehran struggle for control of Strait of Hormuz Reuters.

articles.title: Japan, Philippines aim to fast-track transfer of navy destroyers
articles.summary: Japan and the Philippines aim to quickly transfer navy destroyers. The move is part of their defense cooperation, with the details of the transfer being finalized. Japan, Philippines aim to fast-track transfer of navy destroyers.

articles.title: Japan pivots Indo-Pacific strategy toward Southeast Asia
articles.summary: Japan's Indo-Pacific strategy now prioritizes energy security, critical minerals, and ASEAN resilience, following a visit by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to Vietnam. The updated strategy aims to strengthen ties with Southeast Asian nations.

articles.title: Spain Logs Hottest April Since Records Began In 1961
articles.summary: Spain recorded its hottest April since 1961, with temperatures reaching 15C. This surpasses the previous record set in 2023. The previous record was set in 2023 at 15C, the agency said.

articles.title: School Bullies To Face Caning Under New Guidelines In Singapore
articles.summary: Singapore's new guidelines allow school bullies to face caning, with offenders facing between one and three strokes of the cane. The move aims to address bullying in schools. Under the guidelines, offenders could face between one and three strokes of the cane.

articles.title: DRC protest in support of US sanctions against former president
articles.summary: Thousands protested in the Democratic Republic of Congo in support of US sanctions against former president Joseph Kabila. The sanctions were imposed in response to human rights abuses. DRC protest in support of US sanctions against former president.

articles.title: U.S. insists Iran ceasefire not over despite attacks in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: The US insists that a ceasefire with Iran remains in place despite recent attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. The US has called on Iran to adhere to the ceasefire agreement.

articles.title: US, Iran, UAE trade Hormuz attack claims: What we know
articles.summary: The US, Iran, and UAE exchanged accusations over an attack on the Hormuz Strait, with experts warning that the claims and counterclaims could hinder diplomatic efforts to ease tensions between the US and Iran. The US and Israel have been at odds with Iran.

articles.title: Israel extends detention of Gaza flotilla activists, lawyers say
articles.summary: Israel extended the detention of two Gaza flotilla activists, prompting their lawyers to appeal the decision and accuse the state of lawlessness. The lawyers will challenge the extension in court. The activists were being held in Israeli custody.

articles.title: ‘US aims to protect its ships’: Pete Hegseth warns Iran of ‘overwhelming firepower’
articles.summary: Pete Hegseth warned Iran of the US's "overwhelming firepower" and said the US aims to protect its ships. Hegseth's comments come amid rising tensions between the US and Iran. ‘US aims to protect its ships’: Pete Hegseth warns Iran of ‘overwhelming firepower’.

articles.title: US and Bahrain push UN-backed action for Hormuz as Washington seeks maritime coalition
articles.summary: The US and Bahrain are pushing for UN-backed action to secure the Hormuz Strait, as Washington seeks to build a maritime coalition. The effort aims to stabilize the region. US and Bahrain push UN-backed action for Hormuz as Washington seeks maritime coalition Reuters.

articles.title: India, Japan hold key meeting on healthcare in Delhi
articles.summary: India and Japan held a meeting on healthcare in Delhi, focusing on strengthening health systems and promoting innovation. The cooperation is guided by a Memorandum of Cooperation in healthcare and wellness.

articles.title: From Bilateralism to Multilateralism: Washington’s Push for Strategic Stability Through the P5
articles.summary: The US is shifting from bilateral to multilateral approaches for strategic stability through the P5, a group of five nuclear-armed states. Washington aims to foster cooperation among the P5 members, comprising China, France, Russia, the UK, and the US, to address global security challenges.
